html:
The Sunflower movement was a protest in which students and activists occupied Taiwan's parliament, the Legislative Yuan in Taipei, from 18 March to 10 April 2014.

They opposed a trade in services agreement with the People's Republic of China, which the ruling Kuomintang had pushed through committee in seconds. They feared it would put Taiwan's media and economy under Beijing's sway. Hundreds of thousands rallied outside. The occupation ended when the speaker promised a law to oversee such deals, and the pact was never passed.

The movement brought a new generation into politics. New parties were born, and the Kuomintang lost badly in local elections that year and the presidency to Tsai Ing-wen in 2016. Activists in Hong Kong began the Umbrella Movement months later. It marked the rise of a Taiwanese rather than Chinese identity among the young, a long way from the retreat of 1949.
sum: The Sunflower movement was a protest in which students and activists occupied Taiwan's parliament, the Legislative Yuan in Taipei, from 18 March to 10 April 2014.
